I need you to create the Strategy tab.... For context, here's the article regarding this app I'm building... I'm just building a mock up. 
```This week, 150,000 AI agents started posting on their own social network. They created a religion. They're debating whether to hide conversations from humans. OpenClaw - the framework powering it - hit 100,000 GitHub stars in 72 hours. IBM, Cisco, Forbes, Wired - everyone's covering it.

While the tech world watches AI agents philosophize, I built a legal defense system.


This is personal to me. Real freaking person. 
I've been through the system. Multiple times. I've had public defenders who couldn't remember my name. I've had private attorneys drain my savings and still fumble the basics. I've sat in courtrooms watching lawyers flip through paperwork while my future hung in the balance.

So I started doing my own research. Case law. Precedents. Opposition research. I'd stress-test my arguments at 2am, playing both sides, finding every weakness before the prosecutor could.

W's kept stacking.

Not because I'm smarter than lawyers. Because information wins cases. And I was willing to do the research they weren't.

The System Wasn't Built for Us. So I Built Something Better. 

And please while we read then, look up every piece of tech that I mention. No intel gatekeeping. I'm putting it all out there. 


Now let me show you what I built.
OpenClaw lets you run multiple AI agents as independent sessions. Each agent has its own identity file (called a SOUL.md file), its own memory, its own scheduled wake-ups, its own tools. They share a database so they can see each other's work. They communicate through @mentions. They wake up every 15 minutes to check for tasks, do their work, then go back to sleep.

This isn't a chatbot. This is a team.

Discovery runs in the cloud. I spin up an instance for less than $150 a year. Your case files live in a secure environment. The agents work around the clock.

Here's the squad:
Case Law Agent (session: agent:caselaw:main) Wakes every 15 minutes. Searches legal databases. Finds precedents in your jurisdiction. Tracks how similar charges were decided. Documents everything with citations. When it finds something relevant, it posts to the shared case board and @mentions the Strategy Agent.

Opposition Agent (session: agent:opposition:main) Builds the prosecutor's case better than they will. Every piece of evidence. Every angle of attack. Every witness vulnerability. You see their playbook before trial. Runs hundreds of adversarial scenarios stress-testing what the other side might do.

Strategy Agent (session: agent:strategy:main) Synthesizes everything. Takes the research from Case Law, the attack vectors from Opposition, and builds defense frameworks. Finds your weak points. Suggests alternatives. When it identifies a gap, it assigns research tasks back to Case Law.

Prep Agent (session: agent:prep:main) Runs mock cross-examinations. Asks the questions that would make you stumble. Simulates different prosecutor styles. Keeps drilling until you don't flinch.

Receipts Agent (session: agent:documents:main) This is the agent that cooks. It creates all the documents. It takes what the agents provides - the framework, the cases, the weak points - and packages it all. Creates the motion, the brief, the memorandum, the subpoena 😈. Every citation linked. Every argument formatted for court. When Opposition challenges a particular angle, Receipts pulls the source material and generates the counter-documentation. 

They agents share a long context memory thanks to OpenClaw. When CaseLawAgent finds a relevant precedent, Opposition immediately tests whether the prosecution could distinguish it. When Strategy identifies a weakness, it creates a task for #CaseLawAgent to find supporting cases. They @mention each other, 'hey fam... come check this out'. They build on each other's work.

While you're sleeping, your Research Agent woke up at 3:47am, found a 2019 appellate decision that could be relevant, posted it to the case board, and tagged Strategy for review.

That's the disruption. Not "AI helps with research." Autonomous agents collaborating on your defense 24/7 while you live your life.

Minimize image
Edit image
Delete image

Add a caption (optional)

Let me address the skeptics.
"AI hallucinates. You can't trust it for legal work."

Literally every citation gets verified. This is not the early ChatGPT days with amateur lawyers who have nothing to lose. The agents provide sources - case numbers, court names, dates. Cross-referenced against legal databases. If it can't be verified, it gets flagged. This isn't ChatGPT freestyling. Our people have a lot to lose and it won't happen on our watch. Structured research with receipts.

"This isn't legal advice."

Honestly. Beat it... Neither is a paralegal researching case law. Neither is you spending 40 hours in a law library. Information isn't advice. I'm giving defendants, families, pro'se litgants the same research tools prosecutors take for granted.

"It's too technical for regular people."

This is where my experience changes the game. I've been on both sides. I understand the urban demongraphic. I have made it as easy as snapping pics of your documents, forwarding the emails from your PD/Lawyer, or taking screenshots. You describe your situation. The agents do the rest. You see a dashboard with your case, the research findings, the suggested strategies. You don't need to understand cron jobs to benefit from them, you just get text messages with your agents telling you, "Hey Nicole... We got something major that may shift your case.".

"Lawyers will come after you."

Come see me. They call me the 50 cent of AI... and there is NOTHING I would want more is the publicity of me beating them in court. I'm simply providing research tools and leveling the score. Legal information has never been restricted. What's restricted is representing someone in court. I'm not doing that. I'm giving people the ability to be prepared - something the system actively discourages because unprepared defendants take plea deals.


Who is this for?
The mother who just got that call. Stomach dropped. Doesn't know who to call.

The father in a custody battle against someone with deeper pockets, or an alternative agenda. Knows he's a good parent but can't afford to prove it the way the system demands.

The 19-year-old arrested for a weed pen on campus. First offense. About to get a record that follows him for decades.

The family scrambling to make bail while trying to understand why the public defender has 7 minutes for their case.

Everyone who's felt like the legal system wasn't designed for them.

It wasn't.

But autonomous agents don't care about your income bracket. Research doesn't require a retainer. And a team of AI working your case 24/7 costs less than one hour with a lawyer.


The same week AI agents are building religions, I have agents pulling case precedents that could keep someone out of prison.

Discovery isn't replacing lawyers. It's giving everyone access to the research that determines whether you win or lose.

My DMs are open. I've been impacted by the same system I'm trying to save others from. 

If you're in a situation where you need this, let's talk.

If you want to build something similar for your community, let's chop it up. 

If you want to size me up on the technology behind this, if I understand what true orchestration of agents are, what LangChain or swarm technology is... let's dance. Ask me about state management across distributed agent contexts, ask me about deterministic replay for audit trails in multi-agent workflows, ask me about prompt caching vs. context window optimization when orchestrating 5+ agents with shared memory. Come see me. Because that's what separates "I built an AI assistant" from "I built a legal defense system that 5 agents are actively working 24/7 on your case, and every decision can be reconstructed.

The system won't fix itself.

But we can build around it.

My name is Micah Berkley. I have dedicated my entire life to helping my people. Grew up in group homes and foster care. Found his birth family at 30 years old. And yes. I've know the system. Didn't stop me from getting a Ivy league education, working at Google and demonlishing the limits of technology for our community. I'm showing the world we ALL can eat and we ALL can live comfortable lives. (micahberkley.com) ```
